review.review: The initiating disruption was an unidentified-scroll experiment, not the final fly fallback. Decision 833 (selection line 2357, accepted line 2358) read ODAL at full health with a staff at 1/5. The accepted transition moved the hero from 538 to 842; the next public observation explicitly reported teleportation and showed an awake crab and sleeping enemies. The remaining cast was spent, followed by physical combat, retreats and escalating multi-enemy pressure. Decision 879's accepted transition at line 2547 reduced HP from 2 to 0; the evidence does not identify the fatal attacker. The selecting chain reaches tools/consumable_tactics.py:58-104 through the combat-consumable controller. Its quiet-location and health checks admit deliberate unknown-scroll discovery, but do not establish readiness for random displacement. An isolated fresh-policy helper probe matches decision 833; this is not reconstructed runtime memory or validation of earlier selections. Post-death item identities were not used. No patch or regression is supplied: the source explains the initiating choice, but this recording does not establish a justified charge threshold, admitted preparation sequence or safe replacement identification/escape action. Adding such a threshold or disabling discovery globally would be speculative. Mandatory progression and hazard checks remain unchanged. The unchanged-source suite passed 1569 tests with 4 skipped; there is no candidate or red/green regression claim. The recorded source diff is empty.
review.learnings: A quiet starting square does not make unknown-scroll discovery safe: displacement can expose a nearly depleted Mage to fresh enemies. Evaluate bounded discovery readiness and preparation using public resources, without assuming potion identities or certifying survival from a larger charge reserve alone.
